- `sample_backlog.md`: a public, fictional §4 (a tool-lending library; 21 live stories and 2 tombstones in 4 epics). It carries every format variant the parser handles: `### E<n> Name`, `### E<n>: Name` and `### E<n> — Name` headings, plain and qualified tags (`[MVP; note]`, `[Lite: note]`), an empty core, a story with no text at all, nested sub-bullets, a table, `US-x.y`/`§x`/`(G1)`/`(P2)` references, a `— merged into US-x: reason` and a `— removed: reason` tombstone, and US-1.5 filed under E3. `TESSELINT_SOURCE` points at it in every offline test; `tests/test_sample_backlog.py` covers it.
- `private/fixtures/section4_2026-09-26.md` (gitignored, not in the public tree): §4 of a private product backlog (176 live stories, 3 tombstones), sha256 `b2dd2ef8cf7bd67fe151a1ca270f310efe3691fc58a41b1d7f1208a90611b14c`. Tests that need it take the `real_section4` fixture or call `require_section4()` and skip when it is absent. They pin its wording by short sha256 digests, never by text.
- `jev_bodies.json`, real Jev response bodies from the probes in `research/`: `choice_rel` (rel.v1 wording), `noul_atomic_v1`, `multi_rel_related_sim` (three answers), `error_400_too_many_choices`, `key_usage` (the `data` of `GET /api/v1/key`).
- `noul_atomic_v2` is reconstructed: its answer and usage are real (from the atomicity probe, US-1.10); the envelope copies the real one. Every `id` is replaced by a `FIXTURE` placeholder.
- Answers sit under the request key (`rel`, `atomic`); probabilities may be JSON ints (`0`); `usage.cost` = `input_tokens` × 4.2e-8.
- `ui/`: the synthetic run fixture of the web UI (see `ui/MANIFEST.md`).
